name: Nanotube overhead power line
subtitle: a lighter power line that carries more current

effects.effect: rolled-up carbon sheets are stronger than steel and conduct like metal

effect: rolled-up carbon sheets are stronger than steel and conduct like metal
how: Clean power is stuck waiting for new transmission lines, and existing lines sag and overheat when pushed harder. A cable spun from carbon nanotubes conducts like metal at a fraction of copper's weight and is stronger than steel, so old towers could carry several times more current without sagging.
obstacle: Nanotube yarn still conducts only about a fifth as well as copper, and costs far more to make.
why: Nanotube wires appear in aerospace cabling; no power line uses them.
real: CNT-enhanced overhead conductors exist as simulations, patents and a Mitacs/bbcp research project; field trials found only for carbon-fibre-core conductors.
